Sewer Zama Zama's

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Did you know there was hidden treasure in the sewers of Johannesburg? Called "Sewer Rats," or "Sewer Zama Zamas" we follow a team who find the things we lose down the drains in order to make a living.

Unique Selling Point:
We have footage of Zama Zama's doing this already. We have verified that they are real and not just a myth. The city of joburg is also going to go down with us and let us see the damage caused first hand.

Summary:
In the sewage tunnels in Johannesburg is a trove of hidden treasure (items of value like jewellery or money), sifting through the sewage, storm water and everything else… are Zama Zama’s. There are various ways that they do this: They block the sewage pipe so that it overflows causing it to flood – then sift through it by adding sand to the water to dry it, or use gold pans sifting through the water for valuables, another method is to open sewage infrastructure like manholes, block to water flow if the manhole is full, or go through it with a magnet.
We have several videos of how this is done. “Minister” is a sewer Zama Zama. He was retrenched in 2010 from his job as a plumber. He couldn’t find another job, and didn’t want to do commit a crime, and so thought outside the box. He noticed that as a plumber items often went down the drain and he would have to retrieve them so he began doing this. He said it’s a dirty job, and sometime he can come out with nothing, but more often than not he finds all sorts of treasures that flow down the pipes. He has found watches, rings, necklaces, cell phones, knives, guns, cutlery etc and then cleans them and sells them.
There are obvious risks – health being one of them. The faecal matter contains ecoli and other pathogens that can be deadly if it infects an open cut or is consumed. Another is the risk of drowning or being caught by a current and being dragged under. Others are that when you retrieve your items you could be attacked for them – as is the situation with Gold Zama Zama’s.


Further information:
This underground maze is a dangerous one, but damage caused by this activity to the infrastructure is also costing the Joburg Water millions. They have offered to take us into the sewage pipes to see for ourselves. We have a meeting set up with next week Wednesday to discuss how we do this. But I asked if we can do it on Friday, and they said yes.
They will show us the extent of what’s down there, and give us evidence on the damage caused by the Zama Zama’s. The city is implementing new sewer lines, but the damage caused is costing millions of rands to fix.

Press Release:


Sewer Zama Zamas
If you want to know what poverty smells like, you have to go down one of Johannesburg’s sewers. It’s not for the faint-hearted, but it’s the life of destitute sewer zama zamas who brave exposure to chemicals, disease and flooding to find hidden treasure like jewellery, flushed down suburban toilets. Carte Blanche joins two expert sewer zama zamas to find out why they do it.
Producer: Sasha Schwendenwein
Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli
Watch the trailer


Script:


First it was Gold Zama Zama’s, next they were after Chrome… and now as South Africa is gripped by poverty, desperate Zama Zama’s head into Johannesburg’s Sewers to seek the hidden treasure that lies beneath it.
Minister: “I used to find rings, spoons, money - R2, R5.”
When plumber Timothy Sihkosana – known as “Minister” – was retrenched in 2010, he resorted to extraordinary measures to feed his 3 children.
Min: “No work, you try and make a plan, you get what you can get.”
He pops the heavy manhole lid and the noxious sewage fumes waft upwards.
Minister: “Smells like dinner... You what I’m doing here, I’m trying to catch a fish here. Whatever I get, it’s coming up here (shows us) and I take it like this. I’ve got a magnate that I use to catch the money with it.”
An hour passes without any catches.
Minister: “Been trying a long time here…Really, if I can find something… (sigh). I’ll sleep with a hungry stomach hey.”
Minister leaves empty handed...


In nearby Diepsloot Township, he visits his favourite hunting spot.
LINK: “IF YOU THINK YOU’RE HAVING A CRAPPY DAY AT WORK, THAT’S NOTHING ON ME…LETS SEE WHAT WE FIND… IF THERE’S ANY TREASURE WHATSOEVER…. OMG THE SMELL!”
Minister drops his magnate into the water, and instantly finds success!
LINK: “WE’VE FOUND A COUPLE OF TEASPOONS, WE FOUND A KNIFE. MINISTER HAS TO SIFT THROUGH ALL OF THIS, USING HIS BARE HANDS.”
Minister: “I take the spoons into the scrap yard – 1, 20 litre, and I can get money…”
Mac: “How much do you get out of that?”
Min: “R80 – R100 rands.”
Mac: “And what do with R80?”
Min: “Some milk and maize, some bread yes.”
LINK: “IT’S INCREDIBLY HOT, AS YOU CAN SEE HOW I’M SWEATING; IT’S ALSO VERY, VERY DANGEROUS, AS AT ANY MOMENT IT COULD FILL UP WITH WATER.”
Craig: “There is a reason we invented sewers, because people got ill, so the idea was to invent a water closet to get the sewage out of the bedroom, into a flushable system and away from people.”
Associate Professor Craig Sheridan is the director of WITS University’s Centre in Water and Research Development. He says the pathogens Minister is exposed to are a hidden hazard.
Craig Sheridan: “If there were gases you’d start to asphyxiate, you could pass out and die. You may very well be exposed to pathogenic organisms so these are things like bacteria, viruses, worms, and it can be things like cholera, typhoid fever, and they’re really not good for you.”
LINK: “THIS IS UNBELIEVABLE, BUT IT’S ALSO THE SAD REALITY FOR SOME PEOPLE HAVE TO DO, AND THE LENGTHS THAT THEY HAVE TO GO TO, JUST TO BE ABLE TO FEED THEIR FAMILIES.”
Some “search” methods used by Sewer Zama Zama’s – like this man - requires them to purposefully block a drain so it floods. Isaac Dhludhlu from Johannesburg Water says sometimes the drains are blocked by human negligence, but this time the Sewer Zama Zama’s have broken the city’s infrastructure.
Isaac: “It is illegal to go into a manhole, what happens if you drown in there, or you leave it open and the kids fall in there.”
LINK: WE’VE COME TO SOWETO WITH THE JOBURG WATER TEAM, NOW THERE’S ABOUT 12,000 KM OF INFRASTRUCTURE FOR SEWAGE ALL AROUND JOHANNESBURG, AND THIS IS AN INDICATION OF WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THE ZAMA ZAMA’S BLOCK THE DRAINS, AS YOU CAN SEE IT’S QUITE A MESS.
Isaac: “So we’ve got out jet valve machine here, which will then also pump a lot of water into the system to make sure that whatever blockage is inside there can be pushed out.”
LINK: “ALL OF THIS MANPOWER CAN TAKE 3 DAYS JUST TO UNBLOCK ONE SEWER COSTING THE CITY MILLIONS OF RANDS.”
After 3 hours of draining the waste water, it’s time to see what blocked the sewer.
LINK: “IT’S A DIRTY JOB BUT SOMEBODY’S GOT TO DO IT.”
A wad of cloth used to block this manhole is evidence of the constant battle the city must wage against Zama Zama’s who break infrastructure – this contrasts with Minister’s method of scavenging, which causes no damage.
Mac: “What are some of these things here?”
Min: “Spoons!”
Mac: “We’ve also got a couple of coins here, 50c, R1, R1.50. There’s a couple of 20cents.”
Minister arrives home exhausted…He has a soapy bucket bath... and takes his frustrations out on the boxing bag behind his broken-down car…He knows his family’s survival depends on him returning to the sewers tomorrow.
